desc:
Some leaks appear along a straight pipe at the positions listed in points (several leaks may share a position). You have an unlimited supply of identical repair planks, each of length length. A plank laid with its left end at position x seals every leak at positions from x to x + length, inclusive. Planks may be placed at any real position and may overlap.

Return the minimum number of planks needed to seal all leaks. If there are no leaks, return 0.

points = [4, 1, 9, 2, 6, 5], length = 3  ->  3

Planks at 1 (covers 1, 2, 4), at 5 (covers 5, 6) and at 9 (covers 9).
constraints: The points are in no particular order and may repeat
hints: Think about the leak that is furthest to the left. Some plank has to cover it. Where is the best place for that plank?
Moving the plank further left never helps, because there is nothing to the left of that leak. So put the plank's left end exactly on the leftmost leak.
Sort the points. Start a plank at the first unsealed point, skip every point up to start + length, and repeat with the next unsealed point.
editorial: Sort the positions. The leftmost leak must be sealed by some plank, and sliding that plank to the right until its left end touches the leak can only make it cover more leaks on the right side without losing any (nothing lies left of the leak). So an optimal solution can always start with a plank whose left end is at the leftmost leak. That plank seals every leak up to first + length. Remove them and repeat: this exchange argument shows the greedy choice is safe at every step.

Implementation: walk through the sorted array once with a pointer; whenever the current point is beyond the end of the last plank, open a new plank at this point and set its end to point + length. Sorting costs O(n log n), the scan is O(n).
